name: Femur
description: Distal femur: medial and lateral condyles joined anteriorly by the trochlea and separated posteriorly by the intercondylar notch. Adult epiphyseal marrow is fatty, the metaphysis may hold patchy red marrow, and a thin smooth line marks the closed physis; focal edema straddling a closing adolescent physis is physiologic.

normal_values.trochlear_depth: more than 3 mm on axial, 3 cm above the joint line; 3 mm or less is dysplasia
normal_values.lateral_trochlear_inclination: 11° or more on the highest axial image with trochlear cartilage; below 11° indicates dysplasia
normal_values.lateral_femoral_notch_depth: 1.5 mm or less on sagittal; deeper supports an ACL tear

variants_pitfalls: Red marrow in the metaphysis is common (over half of women, under a sixth of men, many marathon runners): patchy, isointense to or brighter than muscle on T1, sparing the epiphysis. Darker than muscle, epiphyseal extension or cortical breach needs workup.

Cortical irregularity (cortical desmoid): a saucer-shaped posterior cortical defect with a dark rim, almost always at the medial gastrocnemius attachment, in 9–27% of adolescents. Leave it alone; it is not for biopsy.
In children, irregular posterior condylar ossification (about 22%) mimics OCD: favor a variant when it is posterior, cartilage is intact and there is no marrow edema.
